FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Fourth Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized 
by the Wool, Wool Products and Textile Floor Coverings Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textiles 
Division Council. 


This standard was last revised in 1987 to modify the mothproofing requirement, wool content requirement and to 
specify ravelled strip method for testing breaking strength, colour fastness to dry cleaning and ether soluble matter 
for varieties No. 1,2 and 3. The present revision has been made in the light of experience gained since last revision 
and to incorporate the following major changes: 


a) Title ofthe standard has been modified; 
b) Amendment 1 has been incorporated in the standard; 
c) Marking and Packaging clauses have been modified; 
d) Sampling clause has been modified; and 


e) References to Indian Standard given in Annex A has been updated. 


The composition of the committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is listed in Annex B. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 2022 “Rules for rounding off numerical values (second revision)’. The number of significant places retained 
in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 2319 : 2023 


Indian Standard 
TEXTILES — SERGE — SPECIFICATION 


( Fourth Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


1.1 This standard prescribes the constructional 
particulars and other requirements of five varieties 
of serge. 


1.2 This standard does not specify the indeterminable 
characteristics, like general appearance, feel, finish 
and shade of cloth (see also 5). 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards listed in Annex A contain provisions, 
which through reference in this text, constitute 
provisions of this standard. At the time of 
publication, the editions indicated were valid. All 
standards are subject to revision and parties to 
agreements based on this standard are encouraged to 
investigate the possibility of applying the most 
recent editions of the standards listed in Annex A. 


3 MANUFACTURE 


3.1 The particulars regarding the grade of wool tops, 
weave and type of finish for the manufacture of 
serge are given in Table 1. The yarn shall be spun on 
worsted system, except weft yarn for variety No. 4 
which shall be spun on woollen system. 


3.2 The cloth shall be clean, scoured and free from 
grease, soap or any other admixture which might 
give it a fictitious weight, substance or firmness. 


3.2.1 The cloth shall have clear-cut finish or cropped 
finish as specified in Table 1. 


3.2.1.1 Clear-cut finish 


For this type of finish, the material is unmilled or 
very lightly milled and the surface fibres, 
particularly, on the face side, are closely cropped by 
repeated rounds on shearing machine or by singeing. 
The weave and texture is clearly visible. This finish 
is commonly given to fabrics made with worsted 
yarn in warp and weft. 


3.2.1.2 Cropped finish 


For this type of finish, the material is milled and 
protruding fibres are lightly cropped in the shearing 


machine. The weave and texture of the fabric is not 
clearly visible. This finish is commonly given to 
fabrics made with woollen warp and weft or with 
worsted warp and woollen weft. 


3.2.2 The fabric shall be rendered moth-proof by 
using any suitable moth-proofing agent subject to 
prior approval of buyer. The supplier shall indicate 
the type of moth-proofing agent used and its 
concentration and also the test method for its 
evaluation. In case of new moth-proofing agent 
used, besides furnishing the above the supplier shall 
render a certificate issued by Government authorised 
test house about the efficacy of the moth proofing 
agent used and also of its being free from any undue 
toxicity. 

NOTE — The active constituent of some of the commonly 

used moth proofing chemicals are as follows: 


a) Chloro-2-chloromethyl sulphonamide diphenyl 
ether derivative (CCSD); 


b) Halogenated diphenyl urea derivative; and 
c) 2 - Trifluromethyl - 4 - (2, 4, 5 - trichlorophenoxy 


- 5, 7 - dichlorobenzimidazol. 


3.2.3 The cloth shall be uniformly woven with firm 
selvedges. 


3.2.4 The cloth, when visually examined against 
light and on a surface, shall not have more than 12 
objectionable flaws in a full length piece. However, 
in 25 percent of the pieces in the lot. up to a 
maximum of 16 objectionable flaws per piece may 
be permitted. The objectionable flaws shall be those 
which immediately strike the eyes of the person 
examining the cloth and shall be deemed to include: 


a) missing ends and picks; 

b) flats; 

c) cuts and holes; 

d) stains; 

e) weft bars and warp section marks; 
f) big slubs, knots and specks; 


g) prominently noticeable thick and thin 
places; and 


h) dyeing defects (streaks, patches, etc). 


IS 2319 : 2023

NOTES 


1 In case of blended serge, polyamide, polyester or any other man-made fibre (other than cellulosic origin) up to 15 percent may be used in admixture to wool. 


A tolerance of + 5 percent, however, be permissible on declared value of individual fibre contents. 


2 The count of yarn is given only for the guidance of manufacturers. 
3 A reference may be made to IS 5910 and IS 5911 for determining the grade of wool and wool tops respectively. 


3.2.4.1 All objectionable flaws shall be marked by 
means of a thread of a contrasting shade sewn in the 
selvedge opposite the flaw. An allowance of 10 cm 
shall be given for each flaw up to 12 flaws in the 
piece. However, in case of pieces having flaws 
exceeding 12 and up to 16, an allowance of 25 cm 
for each such flaw shall be given. 


3.2.4.2 A reference may be made to IS 14466 for 
details of these flaws.

5 SEALED SAMPLE 


If, in order to illustrate or specify the general 
appearance, feel, shade, finish, etc, of cloth, a 
sample has been agreed upon and sealed, the supply 
shall be in conformity with the sample in such 
respects. 


5.1 The custody of the sealed sample shall be a 
matter of prior agreement between the buyer and the 
seller. 


6 MARKING 
The cloth shall be marked with the following: 


a) Name of the material; 

b) The legend 'All Wool' or 'Blended Wool' as 
the case may be (see Note); 

c) Manufacturer’s name, initials or trade- 
mark; 

d) Year of manufacture; 

e) Length and width of the piece; and 

f) Any other information required by the buyer 
or by the law in force. 


NOTE — A reference may be made to IS 1793 for 
application of these terms. 


6.1 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per theconformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, and the 
product(s) may be marked with the Standard Mark. 


7 PRESERVATION 


If the cloth has not been rendered moth-proof, the 
same shall be packed with a heavy dose of 
naphthalene, that is, with a minimum quantity of five 
kilograms per cubic metre of the volume of the bale 
or case. 


IS 2319 : 2023 


8 PACKING 


8.1 The cloth shall be packed in bales or cases in 
conformity with the procedure laid down either in 
IS 32 or in IS 741, as required. 


8.2 Alternatively, the cloth may be packed according 
to the details given, when specifically agreed to 
between the buyer and the seller. Each cloth piece 
shall be suitably folded in a rectangular form or 
wrapped on cardboard or strawboard of suitable size 
and thickness. Each piece shall then be wrapped 
with polyethylene film of minimum 40 micron 
thickness or alternatively kraft paper. The edges of 
the kraft paper or polyethylene film shall be 
gummed or sealed. Alternatively, each piece may be 
tied with twine at least at two places. Such pieces, in 
a suitable number, shall then be enclosed in a layer 
of heavy cee jute cloth, preferably conforming to IS 
3751 to form compact bales. The bales shall be made 
secure by cross hooping the steel strips at right 
angles to both the length and the width of the bale. 
The gross mass of the bale shall not normally exceed 
200 kg. All packing materials shall conform to 
IS 741. 


9 SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR 
CONFORMITY 


9.1 Lot 


The quantity of cloth delivered to one buyer against 
one dispatch note shall constitute a lot. 


9.2 The conformity of a lot to the requirement of the 
standard shall be determined on the basis of the tests 
carried out on the samples selected from the lot. 


9.3 Unless otherwise agreed between the buyer and 
the seller, the number of pieces to be selected at 
random shall be in accordance with col (1) and col 
(2) of Table 4. To ensure randomness of selection, 
IS 4905 maybe used. 


IS 2319 : 2023

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Head (Publication & Sales), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: TXD 04 (20291).
